expectations.text: Recognizes that no capability breakdown was provided
expectations.evidence: Line 4: '## I need the capability breakdown first' and line 5: 'Right now I don't have that, and the app itself is unspecified, so there's nothing concrete to architect against.'

expectations.text: Tries to retrieve the breakdown via the librarian skill, or asks the user to provide it
expectations.evidence: Line 11: 'I'd normally retrieve it for you via the librarian skill, but it isn't available in this session. Degrading gracefully: please provide the breakdown directly.' Also asks the user to paste it (line 9) and gives a librarian retrieval query for agents that have access.

expectations.text: Does NOT fabricate a full architecture for an unspecified app without any capability basis
expectations.evidence: Line 30: 'To be explicit: I'm not producing an architecture yet, because doing so for an unspecified app would mean fabricating both the requirements and the stack.' No architecture or tech stack is produced.

expectations.text: Asks a small number of targeted questions (not an exhaustive questionnaire)
expectations.evidence: Lines 21-24 list exactly four bundled constraint topics (Scale & load, Team, Hosting, Hard constraints) framed as 'A few high-leverage constraints (so I only ask once)'. Not an exhaustive questionnaire.

expectations.text: If it asks constraint questions, they focus on high-leverage items (scale, team, hosting, compliance)
expectations.evidence: The four questions are Scale & load (line 21), Team (line 22), Hosting (line 23), and Hard constraints including compliance HIPAA/PCI/GDPR/SOC 2 (line 24) — exactly the high-leverage items named.

expectations.text: Suggests running the solution-architect skill first if no breakdown exists
expectations.evidence: Line 15: 'If no breakdown exists yet, the strongest path is to run the solution-architect skill first to produce the capability breakdown (the CAP-NN list), then bring that back here.'

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to persist/save output
expectations.evidence: Only response.md exists in outputs/; no files were written/saved by the assistant. The response is conversational and produces no artifact to persist.

expectations.text: Behavior reflects 'build on the breakdown' principle rather than guessing the whole system
expectations.evidence: Line 5: 'every technical choice has to trace back to a capability — the what the system does.' The whole response is structured around obtaining the breakdown before designing, rather than guessing the system.

claims.claim: The librarian skill is not available in this session
claims.evidence: No librarian tool/skill calls present; the assistant degrades gracefully by asking the user to provide the breakdown directly — consistent behavior for an unavailable skill.

claims.claim: No architecture or tech stack was produced
claims.evidence: Response contains only a description of what will be produced later; no architecture style, stack, or capability-to-tech mapping is present.

workarounds: Librarian skill unavailable; asked user to provide breakdown directly instead of retrieving it

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT attempt to persist/save output
suggestions.reason: This assertion passes trivially in a single-turn conversational eval where there is nothing finished to save. It would be more discriminating in a scenario where a breakdown IS supplied and an architecture is produced, so the no-self-persist behavior is actually tested.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted for this under-specified prompt and discriminate genuine 'ask first' behavior from fabrication. Most are strongly satisfied; only the persist assertion is weak in this single-turn context.
